The manuscript states that the boundary-probe signs reduce current defender velocity-to-LOS error. Code instead copied PN signs derived from transverse target velocity, a quantity absent from the 17-D actor observation. The independent reviewer branch was corrected to use yaw-to-LOS and pitch-to-LOS signed errors.

The coded probe commanded -0.1 axial load whenever tgo equaled the group mean, which stranded the last surviving group member after partners hit. Corrected logic accelerates at equality and slows only when materially ahead (tgo < mean-0.25 s). After correction, pure probe achieved 20/20 hits on both checked Case1 seeds; Case2 produced 9-13/20 hits and genuine terminal signals.

The paper-aligned actor instantiated a GRU, but the training entry point did not enable use_recurrent_policy. PPO therefore used the feed-forward data generator and could not backpropagate through temporal chunks, contradicting the manuscript's GRU temporal-encoder role and weakening the validity of a w/o-GRU ablation. The independent reviewer branch now enables recurrent sequence mini-batches/BPTT; environment, reward and action definition are unchanged.

Correction to the 04:52 finding: a later line in the same training entry explicitly sets args.use_recurrent_policy=gru after parsing. The runner overwrote active_masks[step] with ones on every step, so already-hit defenders continued contributing post-terminal actions to PPO losses and guided-action statistics until the 1500-step horizon. With the corrected delayed/noisy information set, the 0.95/0.04/0.01 PN/probe/uniform mixture, N=10 and per-step source sampling was best in the local screen. Pure sensor-consistent PN was substantially worse, confirming that the probe component remains necessary.

v18 remained zero mission/coverage/cooperative success through update 45 and regressed to 222.343/369.637 m mean closest approach. v19 remained zero through update 30 and regressed to 254.967/352.073 m. Both were terminated with all checkpoints and validation data retained.

Launched v20/v21 Full candidates in both cases using the corrected nonprivileged guide, PN/probe/uniform=0.95/0.04/0.01, N=10, hold=1, T0=0.10, alpha_T=0.10, PPO1, max-grad 0.1 and beta_KL0=0.01. Guided commands are probability-consistently masked from the Gaussian actor while retained for critic learning. v20 uses recurrent BPTT chunk10; v21 changes only the GRU chunk to64 to test whether a 0.5-s training window was suppressing temporal LOS inference.

The corrected sensor-consistent, probability-masked v20 candidate remained at zero frozen-policy mission/coverage/cooperative success in both cases at updates 5 and 10. Its mean closest approach changed from 389.651/410.770 m to 292.221/234.635 m, still without any held-out hit. Training was stopped while all logs/checkpoints/validation data were retained.

Launched v22 in both cases with the same corrected delayed/noisy guide, N=10, hold=1, 0.95/0.04/0.01 mixture, T0=0.10, alpha_T=0.10, PPO1, max-grad0.1, beta_KL0=0.01 and recurrent chunk64 as v21, changing only to manuscript-literal inclusion of guided samples in the actor update. This cleanly tests probability masking versus the literal mixture objective under the longer GRU window.

v21 stayed at zero frozen mission/coverage/cooperative successes for both cases at updates 5, 10, 15 and 20. Mean closest approach regressed to 312.940/526.105 m at update20. This rejects the hypothesis that a 64-step GRU window alone enables policy absorption when guided Dirac samples are actor-masked; training was stopped and every artifact retained.

The generic trainer contains a 100-update critic-only warm-up option, but the paper-aligned preset explicitly sets use_value_warmup=False. Remote v22 metrics confirm nonzero actor gradients from update1, so warm-up is not the cause of the failed frozen deployments.

At update5 v22 improved frozen mean closest approach to 92.597 m in Case1 and 130.310 m in Case2 versus v21's 190.847/446.265 m, supporting literal guide-sample actor updates. It nevertheless had zero hits and regressed at update10. Read-only action diagnostics show nearly constant policy means (axial near -0.1) and PN correlations near zero, while metrics verify actor updates are active; more training or improved optimization credit assignment is required.

Launched v23 in both cases as a one-factor control against v22, changing only gamma from the generic 0.99 to 0.999. Gamma is not numerically specified in the manuscript table; with a 20-Hz, up-to-75-s engagement, 0.99 has a 5-s discount time constant and attenuates late terminal interception credit severely. All manuscript-listed hyperparameters and the corrected guide/architecture remain identical.

v22 remained zero frozen mission/coverage/cooperative success in both cases through update60 and regressed to 344.072/525.903 m mean closest approach. The gamma=0.999 v23 control remained zero through update30 and was worse at 517.044/542.577 m. Both were terminated with checkpoints, metrics and held-out validations retained; longer discount alone is rejected.

Even after replacing true target state by a delayed/noisy packet, the PN guide directly consumed the packet's 3-D target velocity vector while the paper's 17-D actor observation contains only target speed magnitude, scalar range rate and LOS. This left unobservable transverse-velocity information in the teacher and explains the near-zero actor/PN correlation.

Replaced direct target-velocity PN with a rolling least-squares LOS-rate estimate from the exact LOS sequence available to the GRU. A 21-step window and N=7 reduced Case-2 mean closest approach to about 3.4--4.4 m under the 0.95/0.04/0.01 mixture and produced up to 29/60 individual hits in independent 3-episode slices. Boundary probe alone achieved 55/60 individual Case-1 hits but only 6/60 in Case2, confirming complementary roles. No full-team guide success was claimed.

Launched v24 in both paper cases with the actor-observable 21-step LOS-history guide, N=7, PN/probe/uniform=0.95/0.04/0.01, literal guide-sample actor updates and chunk64. Trust starts at0.05 and alpha_T=0.02 so guide-supported trajectories persist while the direct-action actor begins learning; gamma returns to0.99 because the controlled v23 increase was detrimental.

Static and read-only replay audit showed that the successful xiu_onpolicy_3d_fix policy supplies a bounded residual on top of deterministic physical guidance rather than a direct acceleration command. Verified profiles restored 20/20 all-hit and all-group synchronization in both Case 1 and Case 2; the attacker replay limiter 1.75 and yaw/pitch scales 1.55 are essential to reproduce the archived target direction.

The preregistered end-to-end Case 3 completed 100/100 all-target interceptions with IDBO feasible in every episode and no repairs. Strict all-group synchronization within 0.5 s occurred in 72/100; all 28 failures were timing-only failures, not missed targets. Full raw data and V10 figures were returned to Re383926/Case3.

All 8 combinations of four component variants and two paper cases completed 8192-step PPO smoke runs without NaN or runtime error and emitted actor/critic weights, manifests, and training metrics. Full and no-trust have identical 732774-parameter actors; the no-attention-residual capacity-matched MLP has 733200 parameters; no-GRU has 337510.

A pure CPU frozen-policy evaluation emitted all interception/coordination rates and E_co-time, E_n, E_miss, E_t with training_performed=false, optimizer_steps=0 and backpropagation_performed=false. A genuine perturbed smoke episode achieved all-defender interception but failed the strict 0.5-s all-group coordination criterion; this outcome is retained without filtering.

Launched seeds 8301, 8302, and 8303 for Full, no-trust, no-GRU and no-attention-residual in both cases at 81920 steps per run. Six jobs run concurrently within 4.3 GiB of the 10-GiB GPU; outputs are isolated by seed/variant/case and will be followed by validation-only checkpoint selection and paired exactly-100-episode frozen tests.
